title: Psalms Chapter 8 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 8 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 8 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 8.

questions.question: To whom is Psalms 8 dedicated?
options: To the chief Musician upon Gittith
questions.correctAnswer: To the chief Musician upon Gittith
questions.explanation: Psalms 8:1 states that it is "To the chief Musician upon Gittith."

questions.question: According to Psalms 8, how excellent is the LORD's name?
questions.explanation: Verse 1 says, "O LORD our Lord, how excellent is thy name in all the earth!"

questions.question: In Psalms 8, where has God set His glory?
questions.explanation: Verse 1 mentions that God "hast set thy glory above the heavens."

questions.question: From whose mouth has God ordained strength according to Psalms 8?
questions.explanation: Verse 2 states, "Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings hast thou ordained strength."

questions.question: Why has God ordained strength from the mouth of babes and sucklings?
options: Because of thine enemies, that thou mightest still the enemy and the avenger
To praise Him in the temple
To teach the law to Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Because of thine enemies, that thou mightest still the enemy and the avenger
questions.explanation: Verse 2 explains the purpose: "because of thine enemies, that thou mightest still the enemy and the avenger."

questions.question: What does the Psalmist consider in Psalms 8?
options: Thy heavens, the work of thy fingers, the moon and the stars
questions.correctAnswer: Thy heavens, the work of thy fingers, the moon and the stars
questions.explanation: Verse 3 states, "When I consider thy heavens, the work of thy fingers, the moon and the stars, which thou hast ordained."

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 8 says God has set His glory below the heavens.
questions.explanation: Verse 1 says God "hast set thy glory above the heavens," not below.

questions.question: True or False: God uses strength from the mouths of babes and sucklings to silence His enemies in Psalms 8.
questions.explanation: Verse 2 states this clearly: "Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings hast thou ordained strength because of thine enemies."

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 8 describes the moon and the stars as created by men's hands.
questions.explanation: Verse 3 says the heavens, moon, and stars are "the work of thy fingers," meaning God's creation, not man's.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 8 declares the name of the LORD to be excellent in all the earth.
questions.explanation: Verse 1 and again verse 9 affirm "O LORD our Lord, how excellent is thy name in all the earth!"

questions.question: In Psalms 8, what is man crowned with?
questions.explanation: Verse 5 states, "and hast crowned him with glory and honour."

questions.question: According to Psalms 8, man is made a little lower than what?
questions.explanation: Verse 5 says, "For thou hast made him a little lower than the angels."

questions.question: What dominion has God given to man according to Psalms 8?
options: Dominion over the works of God’s hands
questions.correctAnswer: Dominion over the works of God’s hands
questions.explanation: Verse 6 states, "Thou madest him to have dominion over the works of thy hands."

questions.question: According to Psalms 8, what are some of the creatures under man's feet? (Select the one that is NOT mentioned)
questions.explanation: Verses 7 and 8 mention sheep, oxen, beasts of the field, fowl of the air, and fish of the sea, but not lions and serpents explicitly.

questions.question: In Psalms 8, which comes first: God setting His glory above the heavens or God ordaining strength from babes and sucklings?
options: God setting His glory above the heavens
God ordaining strength from babes and sucklings
questions.correctAnswer: God setting His glory above the heavens
questions.explanation: Verse 1 mentions God setting His glory above the heavens before verse 2 speaks of strength from babes and sucklings.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 8 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 8 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 8:4, what question does the Psalmist ask that reflects on human significance?
options: What is man, that thou art mindful of him?
Who made the heavens and the earth?
Why do the stars shine so brightly?
questions.correctAnswer: What is man, that thou art mindful of him?
questions.explanation: Psalms 8:4 directly asks, 'What is man, that thou art mindful of him?' showing the Psalmist's wonder at God's attention to humanity.

questions.question: How does Psalms 8:5 describe the position of man in creation?
options: Made a little lower than the angels and crowned with glory and honour
questions.correctAnswer: Made a little lower than the angels and crowned with glory and honour
questions.explanation: Psalms 8:5 states that man was made 'a little lower than the angels' and crowned with glory and honour, emphasizing man's exalted status.

questions.question: What authority is given to man according to Psalms 8:6?
options: Dominion over the works of God's hands and all things put under his feet
Dominion only over the beasts of the field
No authority, but to serve creation
questions.correctAnswer: Dominion over the works of God's hands and all things put under his feet
questions.explanation: Psalms 8:6 explains that man was given dominion over God's works, with all things under his feet, indicating stewardship and authority.

questions.question: What biblical truth about humility can be drawn from Psalms 8:4-5?
options: Though man is small compared to the heavens, God honors him with glory
Man is insignificant and forgotten by God
God does not care about human affairs
questions.correctAnswer: Though man is small compared to the heavens, God honors him with glory
questions.explanation: Verses 4-5 contrast man's seeming smallness with God's mindful honor, teaching humility balanced with dignity given by God.

questions.question: According to Psalms 8:6-8, which of the following is NOT mentioned as under man's dominion?
questions.explanation: Verses 6-8 list various creatures under man's dominion but the stars and moon are part of God's creation, not under man's authority.

questions.question: How does Psalms 8:2 teach us about God using unexpected sources of strength?
options: God ordains strength from the mouth of babes and sucklings to silence enemies
Strength only comes from the powerful and wise
Babes and sucklings have no role in spiritual strength
Enemies are stronger than God's people
questions.correctAnswer: God ordains strength from the mouth of babes and sucklings to silence enemies
questions.explanation: Psalms 8:2 shows God uses even the weakest, like babes, to demonstrate strength and silence opposition, encouraging trust in God's ways.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 8:5 states that man was made equal to the angels.
questions.explanation: Psalms 8:5 says man was made a little lower than the angels, not equal, highlighting man's honored position but still subordinate to angels.

questions.question: What does Psalms 8:9 emphasize about God's name?
options: How excellent is thy name in all the earth
God's name is only in heaven
questions.correctAnswer: How excellent is thy name in all the earth
questions.explanation: Psalms 8:9 repeats the praise of God's excellent name throughout the earth, encouraging reverence and worship.

questions.question: How does Psalms 8:6 connect to Psalms 8:7 and 8 in describing man's role?
options: Man has dominion over all creatures listed in verses 7 and 8
Man only rules over sheep and oxen
Man is ruled by the beasts of the field
Man has no authority over creation
questions.correctAnswer: Man has dominion over all creatures listed in verses 7 and 8
questions.explanation: Verse 6 introduces man's dominion which is detailed in verses 7 and 8 with specific creatures, showing comprehensive stewardship.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 8:4-6 suggest that human worth is based on achievements rather than God's mindful care.
questions.explanation: These verses emphasize God's mindful care and honor toward man, not human achievements, as the basis for worth.

questions.question: A believer feels insignificant compared to the vast universe. Based on Psalms 8:3-5, what biblical truth encourages them?
options: Despite the vast heavens, God is mindful of man and honors him with glory and honor
The universe is more important than man
Man should fear the vastness and distance from God
Humans are unimportant in God's plan
questions.correctAnswer: Despite the vast heavens, God is mindful of man and honors him with glory and honor
questions.explanation: Verses 3-5 contrast the greatness of the heavens with God's special attention and honor toward man, providing encouragement.

questions.question: What does Psalms 8:6 teach about human responsibility?
options: Man is given dominion over God's works and responsible stewardship
Man is free to exploit creation without care
Man has no role in creation
questions.correctAnswer: Man is given dominion over God's works and responsible stewardship
questions.explanation: Dominion implies stewardship and responsibility over creation, as expressed in Psalms 8:6.

questions.question: What role do the 'babes and sucklings' play according to Psalms 8:2 in the battle against enemies?
options: They are ordained by God to demonstrate strength and silence enemies
They are a distraction to the enemy
questions.correctAnswer: They are ordained by God to demonstrate strength and silence enemies
questions.explanation: Psalms 8:2 teaches that God uses even the weakest, like babes, to show strength and defeat adversaries.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 8:7-8 describe the scope of man's dominion as including the fish of the sea and the birds of the air.
questions.explanation: Verses 7 and 8 explicitly list fish and birds among the creatures under man's dominion.

questions.question: What does Psalms 8 teach about the relationship between God's majesty and human humility?
options: God's majesty is vast, yet He honors humble man with glory and dominion
Humility lowers man far below God's notice
God's majesty demands human fear but no honor
questions.correctAnswer: God's majesty is vast, yet He honors humble man with glory and dominion
questions.explanation: The Psalm contrasts God's majestic heavens with His honoring of man, encouraging humility coupled with trust in God's care (verses 3-6).

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 8 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 8.

questions.question: According to Psalms 8:7, which of the following is NOT mentioned as being under man's dominion?
questions.explanation: Psalms 8:7 lists sheep, oxen, and beasts of the field as under man's dominion, but does not mention serpents.

questions.question: Psalms 8:8 mentions 'the fowl of the air' and what other categories as under man's dominion?
options: Fish of the sea and beasts of the field
Fish of the sea and whatsoever passeth through the paths of the seas
Beasts of the field and cattle
Fowl of the air and creeping things
questions.correctAnswer: Fish of the sea and whatsoever passeth through the paths of the seas
questions.explanation: Psalms 8:8 specifies the fowl of the air, fish of the sea, and whatsoever passeth through the paths of the seas as under man's dominion.

questions.question: What repeated phrase in Psalms 8:1 and 8:9 emphasizes the majesty of God's name?
options: O LORD our Lord, how excellent is thy name in all the earth!
The heavens declare the glory of God
Blessed be the Lord God of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: O LORD our Lord, how excellent is thy name in all the earth!
questions.explanation: Both Psalms 8:1 and 8:9 begin with 'O LORD our Lord, how excellent is thy name in all the earth!' forming an inclusio praising God's name.

questions.question: The dominion given to man in Psalms 8:6 is over the works of whose hands?
questions.explanation: Psalms 8:6 states that man has dominion over the works of God's hands, emphasizing divine creation.

questions.question: In Psalms 8:5, man is made a little lower than whom?
questions.explanation: Psalms 8:5 says man is made a little lower than the angels and crowned with glory and honour.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 8:7 includes 'oxen' as part of the creatures under man's dominion.
questions.explanation: Psalms 8:7 explicitly mentions 'oxen' as part of the creatures subject to man's dominion.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of God's majesty in creation found in Psalms 8?
questions.explanation: Job 38:4-7 describes God’s creation of the heavens and earth, similar to Psalms 8's theme of God’s majesty in creation.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the dominion and lordship of man as crowned with glory and honour, echoing Psalms 8?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:6-8 quotes Psalms 8 to show Jesus' temporary subjection to death and his lordship over creation, reflecting man's crowned glory.

questions.question: What is the literary device called that frames Psalms 8 with the identical phrase in verses 1 and 9?
questions.explanation: The repetition of 'O LORD our Lord, how excellent is thy name in all the earth!' at the beginning and end forms an inclusio, framing the Psalm.

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated 'dominion' in Psalms 8:6 most closely means:
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for dominion ('mashal') means to rule or have authority, as seen in Psalms 8:6 where man is given dominion over creation.

questions.question: Psalms 8:4 asks, 'What is man, that thou art mindful of him?' This reflects which theological theme?
questions.explanation: Psalms 8:4 expresses wonder that God, who made the vast heavens, is mindful of human beings, highlighting their significance despite their smallness.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 8:2 suggests that strength is ordained from the mouths of babes and sucklings to silence enemies.
questions.explanation: Psalms 8:2 says strength is ordained out of the mouths of babes and sucklings because of enemies, but the purpose is to still the enemy and avenger, not silence per se.

questions.question: Which sea creatures are explicitly mentioned in Psalms 8:8 as under man's dominion?
questions.explanation: Psalms 8:8 includes 'the fish of the sea' as among the creatures under man's dominion.

questions.question: What cultural or historical context helps explain the emphasis on dominion over animals in Psalms 8:6-8?
questions.explanation: In the Ancient Near East, kings often claimed dominion over animals and creation as a symbol of their authority, reflected in the Psalm's emphasis on man's dominion.

questions.question: The phrase 'the work of thy fingers' in Psalms 8:3 is an example of what literary device?
questions.explanation: Calling the heavens 'the work of thy fingers' uses metaphor to highlight the intimate and skilled creation by God.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 8 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 8 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is primarily highlighted in Psalms 8:1 through the phrase 'who hast set thy glory above the heavens'?
questions.explanation: Psalms 8:1 emphasizes God's glory set above the heavens, highlighting His transcendence, meaning He is above and beyond all creation.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by the phrase 'Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings hast thou ordained strength because of thine enemies' in Psalms 8:2?
questions.explanation: Psalms 8:2 reveals God's providential use of even the weakest (babes and sucklings) to silence enemies, showing His sovereign care over all circumstances.

questions.question: According to Psalms 8:3, what does the observation of the heavens, moon, and stars reveal about God?
questions.explanation: Psalms 8:3 refers to the heavens as the work of God's fingers, indicating His wisdom in creation.

questions.question: What profound question about humanity's status before God is posed in Psalms 8:4?
options: What is man that God is mindful of him?
questions.correctAnswer: What is man that God is mindful of him?
questions.explanation: Psalms 8:4 questions the significance of humanity given God's vast creation, emphasizing God's gracious mindfulness toward man.

questions.question: Which doctrine is taught by the statement in Psalms 8:5, 'For thou hast made him a little lower than the angels, and hast crowned him with glory and honour'?
options: Doctrine of the Image of God
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of the Image of God
questions.explanation: Psalms 8:5 portrays humanity’s exalted position just below angels, crowned with glory and honor, reflecting the imago Dei—the Image of God.

questions.question: What role does humanity have in creation according to Psalms 8:6?
options: To have dominion over the works of God’s hands
To be servants to the beasts
questions.correctAnswer: To have dominion over the works of God’s hands
questions.explanation: Psalms 8:6 clearly states that God gave man dominion over creation, indicating stewardship responsibility.

questions.question: Which of the following best expresses the scope of dominion given to humanity as described in Psalms 8:7-8?
options: All animals including sheep, oxen, beasts, birds, and fish
Only over the fish of the sea
questions.correctAnswer: All animals including sheep, oxen, beasts, birds, and fish
questions.explanation: Psalms 8:7-8 enumerates the full spectrum of animals under man's dominion—sheep, oxen, beasts, fowl, and fish—showing comprehensive authority.

questions.question: How does Psalms 8:9 reinforce the themes introduced in Psalms 8:1?
options: By repeating the praise of God's name being excellent in all the earth
By describing God's judgment on enemies
By recounting God's covenant with Israel
questions.correctAnswer: By repeating the praise of God's name being excellent in all the earth
questions.explanation: Psalms 8:9 repeats the exaltation of God's name in all the earth, reinforcing His supreme glory as introduced in verse 1.

questions.question: What synthesis of Psalms 8:5 and Psalms 8:6 teaches about the nature and purpose of humanity?
options: Man is created lower than beasts and without purpose
Man is crowned with honor and given dominion to reflect God's glory
Man is destined to be an angelic being
Man is primarily a judge of angels
questions.correctAnswer: Man is crowned with honor and given dominion to reflect God's glory
questions.explanation: Combining Psalms 8:5 and 8:6 shows man’s exalted status crowned with glory and honor and his God-given dominion, indicating humanity’s role to reflect God's glory through stewardship.

questions.question: How do Psalms 8:2 and Psalms 8:9 together highlight the relationship between God’s strength and His glory in creation?
options: God’s strength is limited and His glory is hidden
God’s strength is demonstrated even through the weak, and His glory is declared throughout the earth
God’s glory is only for Israel and strength comes from warfare
God’s strength is unrelated to His glory
questions.correctAnswer: God’s strength is demonstrated even through the weak, and His glory is declared throughout the earth
questions.explanation: Psalms 8:2 shows God ordaining strength through the weak (babes), and Psalms 8:9 praises His excellent name throughout the earth, linking God’s strength and universal glory.

questions.question: Which Christological foreshadowing can be inferred from Psalms 8:6 about dominion and authority?
options: Christ as the Son of Man given all authority over creation
Christ as a prophet without authority
Christ as a suffering servant without dominion
questions.correctAnswer: Christ as the Son of Man given all authority over creation
questions.explanation: Psalms 8:6’s dominion given to 'man' foreshadows Christ, the perfect Son of Man, who has all authority over creation (cf. Matthew 28:18).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that humanity is insignificant and accidental in the universe. What does Psalms 8:4-5 actually teach about humanity’s significance?
options: Humanity is insignificant and forgotten by God
Humanity is made a little lower than angels and crowned with glory and honor
Humanity is equal to animals and has no special role
Humanity is doomed to destruction without hope
questions.correctAnswer: Humanity is made a little lower than angels and crowned with glory and honor
questions.explanation: Psalms 8:4-5 emphasizes God’s mindful regard of man and his exalted status just below angels, countering claims of insignificance.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight about God’s sovereign ordering of creation is taught by combining Psalms 8:3 and Psalms 8:6-8?
options: God’s sovereign hand ordains the heavens and grants humanity dominion over the earth
The heavens are independent of God’s control
questions.correctAnswer: God’s sovereign hand ordains the heavens and grants humanity dominion over the earth
questions.explanation: Psalms 8:3 speaks of God’s handiwork in the heavens and Psalms 8:6-8 shows God’s sovereign grant of dominion to man, revealing ordered creation under God’s control.

questions.question: How does Psalms 8 as a whole contribute to the biblical narrative of redemption and sanctification?
options: It denies humanity’s significance and calls for destruction
It affirms humanity’s exalted role under God’s authority, foreshadowing Christ’s kingdom and the restoration of creation
It focuses only on angelic beings and ignores mankind
It teaches that creation is cursed without hope
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms humanity’s exalted role under God’s authority, foreshadowing Christ’s kingdom and the restoration of creation
questions.explanation: Psalms 8 highlights humanity’s God-given dominion and honor, which points forward to Christ’s reign and the ultimate restoration of all creation (cf. Romans 8:19-21).

questions.question: Which attribute of God is primarily illustrated by His being 'mindful' of man in Psalms 8:4?
questions.explanation: Psalms 8:4 shows God’s mindfulness of humanity, reflecting His intimate attentiveness and loving care beyond mere knowledge.
